module purpose: neorv32_debug_dm accepts DMI transactions and a debug-side bus transaction interface, stores debug control/command/program/data state, and sequences abstract commands with per-hart status tracking. It optionally gates access through an authenticator, drives halt_req_o and ndmrstn_o, and returns status, program, and data values on the DMI and bus response interfaces.

use-case flows.value: authorization decision that gates DMI reads/writes and externally visible halt/reset/status actions
debug-module control settings: dmactive, ndmreset, halt request, resume request, reset acknowledge, and selected hart
abstract command, auto-execution settings, and program-buffer words
start of abstract-command processing from a command write or from auto-execution accesses
command validation, load/store-program preparation, execute-request generation, and bus-side data/acknowledge exchange
reported debug status, control, error, authentication, and hart-state values on DMI reads
stored data-register word and prepared program-buffer words returned on DMI or bus reads
controller, status, control, program, and data state forced to known values when rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: When AUTHENTICATOR is enabled, auth.valid enters from the authenticator sub-unit at line 745 and gates authorized DMI write/read strobes at lines 212-213, halt_req_o at line 500, ndmrstn_o at line 505, and most DMI readback fields at lines 530, 555, 573, 584, 596, 604, and 614. Corrupting this decision changes which debug actions and status reads are allowed; when AUTHENTICATOR is disabled, line 754 forces the decision high.

dm_reg.dmcontrol_dmactive is written from the dmcontrol access at line 433, forces the controller back to its inactive baseline at lines 229-236 when cleared, qualifies halt_req_o and ndmrstn_o at lines 500 and 505, and drives the authenticator enable input at line 743. Integrity of this held setting matters because it decides whether debug actions and state-machine progress are active at all; it is also reported at line 569.

dm_reg.hartsel is written at line 429, decoded into dm_reg.hartsel_dec at line 487, and checked against NUM_HARTS at line 489. This selection routes halt, resume, reset, and execute control at lines 298, 366, 377, 384, and 500, and selects which hart status contributes to DMI status at lines 534-545 and 615; corruption misdirects operations or reports the wrong hart.

dm_reg.halt_req is written from the dmcontrol access at line 426. request_gen then drives halt_req_o from halt_req, the selected-hart decode, dmactive, and authorization at line 500, so integrity requires the selected consumers to receive exactly the intended halt vector; availability is provided by the stored request state between writes.

conceptual assets.concept: Non-debug reset request and tracked reset state
conceptual assets.reasoning: dm_reg.dmcontrol_ndmreset is written at line 430 and drives the external reset output low only under the qualified condition at line 505. hart_status also tracks per-hart reset state from this request and reset acknowledgements at lines 382-385, and that tracked state is reported in dmstatus at lines 534-535. Integrity of both the held request and the tracked reset state matters because they define the reset behavior and the reported reset status.

dm_reg.req_res captures the dmcontrol resume-request bit at line 427, and hart_status turns it into persistent per-hart resume requests at lines 366-369 until acknowledgements clear them. The resulting vector is forwarded for the bus-side consumer at line 501 and can be read back at line 699, so integrity requires the selected harts to receive exactly the requested resume state and availability requires the request to persist until acknowledged.

dm_reg.command is accepted only when the access is to addr_command_c, authorized, not busy, and free of prior error at lines 438-439. The controller then inspects its fields to validate the format at lines 261-265, choose load/store/nop preparation at lines 279-291, and select optional program-buffer use at line 293, so integrity of the stored command is required for correct command interpretation and execution preparation.

dm_reg.abstractauto_autoexecdata and dm_reg.abstractauto_autoexecprogbuf are written at lines 444-446. These settings cause access-triggered autoexec events: dm_reg.autoexec_wr is raised on matching writes at lines 450-454 and dm_reg.autoexec_rd on matching reads at lines 635-639, and either event starts command checking at lines 255-256. Integrity matters because these values decide whether ordinary data/program-buffer accesses become command starts; availability is provided by the held configuration and the generated event flags.

conceptual assets.concept: Abstract-command engine state, dispatch, and error status
conceptual assets.reasoning: dm_ctrl.state sequences the engine through its cases at lines 245-317, dm_ctrl.busy is derived from state at line 339 and blocks command/data/program-buffer accesses at lines 438, 443, 464, 469, 474, 495, and 626, dci.req_exe is issued for the selected hart(s) at line 298 and advances on ack_exe at lines 299-300, and dm_ctrl.cmderr is updated from illegal-state, exception, illegal-command, and access-error conditions at lines 320-331. Integrity of these values matters because they determine command progress, whether new commands may be accepted, and the reported abstractcs status at lines 587-589; availability is provided by the stored sequencer and error state.

conceptual assets.concept: Prepared instruction sequence for abstract command execution
conceptual assets.reasoning: In CMD_PREPARE, dm_ctrl.ldsw_progbuf is built from fixed instruction templates, dataaddr_c, and command fields at lines 279-291; dm_ctrl.pbuf_en captures whether optional program-buffer entries are enabled at line 293; dm_reg.progbuf stores those optional words at lines 465 and 470; and cpu_progbuf assembles the four returned words at lines 508-511. Integrity matters because the bus-side consumer receives exactly this prepared sequence at line 694, and when pbuf_en is low lines 509-510 substitute NOPs instead of the stored program-buffer words.

dci.data_reg is loaded either from an authorized DMI data0 write at lines 495 and 665-666 or from a bus write to the data window at lines 667-668. It is returned on DMI data0 reads at line 605 and on bus reads at line 696, and the prepared load/store command sequence addresses this same data window, so integrity requires both interfaces to observe exactly the stored word and availability requires the word to be preserved until overwritten or reset.

dm_ctrl.hart_halted is updated from ndmreset, halt acknowledgements, and resume acknowledgements at lines 355-360, and dm_ctrl.hart_resume_ack is updated from ndmreset, resume acknowledgements, and new resume requests at lines 373-378. hart_halted is required for command acceptance at lines 266-270, and both states are reported in dmstatus or haltsum at lines 536-545 and 615, so integrity of these stored status vectors matters for both internal command legality and external status reporting.
